answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3, columns 1-3, well away from the central blob.
answer.mechanism: Many first-layer units carry very large weights on the top-left 3x3 patch, with a sign that matches their role in blob sizing. Units 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20 and 29 (positive weights on a large central disc, i.e. large-blob detectors) also have strongly positive weights (+40 to +99) on the patch. Units 5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27 and 30 (background or small-blob units: positive on the periphery, negative on the mid-ring) have strongly negative weights (-40 to -98) on the patch. Layer-2 units with positive output weights collect from the first group and are inhibited by the second: u3 (+67) has weights 0:+43, 2:+84, 4:+89, 8:+92, 10:+94, 5:-98, 27:-90. Likewise u10 (+74), u12 (+41) and u13 (+38). Units with negative output weights, such as u0 (-99), take the opposite pattern (0:-65, 4:-79, 18:-77, 21:+93, 9:+84). A bright patch therefore drives the logit toward class 1 (large blob).
answer.evidence: Patch weights at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 are the largest magnitudes in W1. Unit 4 has 93 49 51 / 98 98 72 / 93 94 55. Unit 20 has 81 90 93 / 77 78 94 / 52 38 91. Unit 5 has -82 -72 -57 / -57 -82 -86 / -76 -98 -98. Unit 14 has -77 -98 -44 and similar. Surrounding pixels (row 0, row 4, column 0, column 4) carry only small noise-level weights, so the feature is a sharply bounded square, not part of the blob template. The patch sign is consistent with each unit's large-blob or small-blob role, and it feeds the same layer-2 pathways that push the logit positive.
answer.main_feature: The model measures how far the bright region extends from the centre. Large-blob units have positive weights on a wide disc or annulus (about rows 5-18, cols 5-18). Small-blob units have negative weights on that annulus and positive weights on the outer background. Their difference sets the logit.
